extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or advanced undergraduates in commutative algebra / algebra
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, characterizations, existence/uniqueness theorems and structural results for primary decomposition, associated primes, module length, and Hilbert functions in Noetherian graded/non-graded settings. Includes localization and filtration behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated primes of Hom
rubrics_metrics.description: Ass(Hom(M, N)) = Supp(M) ∩ Ass(N) for R Noetherian and M,N finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses that M is finitely presented, localization, and that Hom commutes with localization: Hom(M,N)_p = Hom_{R_p}(M_p, N_p). If p ∈ Ass(Hom(M,N)) one gets an injection R/p → Hom(M,N) and hence p ∈ Supp(M) and p ∈ Ass(N). Conversely produce nonzero Hom at p using Nakayama and maps to k(p).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of associated prime under choice of nonzerodivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R Noetherian, p prime, M finitely generated, and x,y ∈ p nonzerodivisors on M. Then p ∈ Ass(M/xM) iff p ∈ Ass(M/yM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof forms exact sequences involving multiplication by x,y and applies Hom(R/p, –), using exactness (Snake Lemma) to compare Hom(R/p, M/xM) and Hom(R/p, M/yM). Shows Hom(R/p, M/xM)=Hom(R/p, M/yM) so associatedness at p does not depend on choice of nonzerodivisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary submodule (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Q is p-primary in M if Ass(M/Q) consists of a single prime p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the defining criterion; equivalently M/Q has exactly one associated prime. Example: a prime ideal p is p-primary because Ass(R/p) = {p}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nilradical of a primary quotient equals the prime
rubrics_metrics.description: If Q is p-primary (R Noetherian, M finitely generated), then p = nil(M/Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses that nil(M/Q) = ∩_{q∈Ass(M/Q)} q; when Ass(M/Q)={p} the intersection is p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of p-primary submodule (Theorem 18.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For R Noetherian, M finitely generated, Q ⊂ M and p := nil(M/Q), the following are equivalent: (1) p is prime and Q is p-primary; (2) p = z.div(M/Q) (the set of zerodivisors on M/Q); (3) given x∈R and m∈M with xm∈Q but m∉Q, necessarily x∈p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: Q is p-primary iff every zerodivisor on M/Q is nilpotent / lies in p, equivalently the 'if xm∈Q and m∉Q then x∈p' condition. Proof relies on relationships between associated primes, nilradical, and zerodivisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for an ideal to be primary (Corollary 18.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For R Noetherian and q a proper ideal with p := √q, q is p-primary iff for x,y ∈ R with xy ∈ q but x ∉ q, necessarily y ∈ p; in that case p is prime and q is p-primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the special-case ideal-version of Theorem 18.4: the multiplicative criterion (if xy ∈ q and x not in √q then y must be in √q) characterizes primary ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of principal prime are primary (Exercise 18.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p = (π) is a principal prime generated by a nonzerodivisor π, then every positive power p^n is p-primary. Conversely, if R is Noetherian and q is p-primary, then q = p^n for some n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First direction: multiplication by π acts nilpotently modulo p^n in the expected way. Converse uses Noetherian hypothesis and primary decomposition structure for ideals in principal-prime case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal nilradical implies primary (Proposition 18.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let p := nil(M/Q). If p is maximal then Q is p-primary (R Noetherian, M finitely generated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because nil(M/Q) = ∩_{q∈Ass(M/Q)} q and a maximal p containing that intersection forces all associated primes to equal p, hence Ass(M/Q)={p}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal-case ideal primary criterion (Corollary 18.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If q is an ideal with p := nil(R/q) maximal, then q is p-primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special case of Proposition 18.9 applied to M=R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of m-primary ideals (Corollary 18.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: For R Noetherian and m maximal, an ideal q is m-primary iff there exists n ≥ 1 with m^n ⊆ q ⊆ m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently q contains a power of the maximal ideal; proof uses nilradical criteria and the fact that m is maximal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection of p-primary submodules is p-primary (Lemma 18.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Q1 and Q2 are p-primary submodules of M, then Q1 ∩ Q2 is p-primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider canonical map M → M/Q1 × M/Q2; kernel is Q1∩Q2 and associated primes of product are subset-union of those of factors (each {p}), so the intersection has single associated prime {p}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary decomposition and minimality (Definition 18.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: A primary decomposition of N⊂M is N = Q1 ∩ ... ∩ Qr with each Qi primary. It is irredundant/minimal if (1) N ≠ ∩_{j≠i} Q_j for each i, and (2) the primes p_i of the Qi are distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over Noetherian rings any primary decomposition can be made irredundant by intersecting components with same prime and discarding unnecessary ones. Irredundant means no primary component can be omitted or replaced by a larger primary component with same prime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated primes of a primary decomposition (Lemma 18.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: If N = ∩_{i=1}^r Q_i is a primary decomposition with Qi p_i-primary, then Ass(M/N) ⊆ {p1,...,pr}. If equality holds and p_i are distinct the decomposition is irredundant; conversely (when R is Noetherian) irredundant implies equality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses injections M/N → ⊕ M/Qi and properties of Ass under injections and unions. This links the set of associated primes of the quotient to the primes appearing in any decomposition and characterizes irredundance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of primes in irredundant decomposition (First Uniqueness, Theorem 18.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: For R Noetherian and M a module, in any irredundant primary decomposition N = ∩ Qi (Qi p_i-primary), the primes p1,...,pr are uniquely determined; they are exactly the distinct associated primes of M/N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate from Lemma 18.18: associated primes of M/N are intrinsic, so the primes appearing in any irredundant decomposition are the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of irredundant primary decomposition (Lasker–Noether, Theorem 18.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Over a Noetherian ring, each proper submodule of a finitely generated module has an irredundant primary decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct Qi for each associated prime p_i of M/N such that Ass(Qi/N)={p_i}, then intersecting these Qi yields N. Existence relies crucially on Noetherian hypothesis to ensure finiteness of associated primes and existence of Qi.

rubrics_metrics.name: a-torsion submodule description (Exercise 18.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: For R Noetherian, a ideal, M finitely generated, define a(M) := { m∈M | a^n m = 0 for some n ≥ 1}. If 0 = ∩ Qi with Qi p_i-primary, then (1) a(M) = ⋂_{a ⊄ p_i} Q_i; (2) a(M) equals the set of m whose support lies in V(a), i.e., those m whose localization at primes not containing a vanish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the a-power-torsion submodule as the intersection of primary components whose primes do not contain a; equivalently elements supported on V(a). Useful for understanding supports and torsion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of a p-primary submodule (Lemma 18.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let S be multiplicative subset. If S ∩ p ≠ ∅ then S^{-1}Q = S^{-1}M and QS = M. If S ∩ p = ∅ then S^{-1}Q is S^{-1}p-primary and QS = φ_S^{-1}(S^{-1}Q) = Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primes in S^{-1}R correspond to primes q in R with S ∩ q = ∅. The behavior of primary components under localization is dictated by whether p meets S. If p meets S the localized quotient vanishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of an irredundant primary decomposition (Proposition 18.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: For R Noetherian, S multiplicative, and an irredundant decomposition N = ∩_{i=1}^r Q_i with Qi p_i-primary, let S ∩ p_i = ∅ for i ≤ h and nonempty for i>h. Then S^{-1}N = ⋂_{i=1}^h S^{-1}Q_i is an irredundant primary decomposition in S^{-1}M, and N_S = ⋂_{i=1}^h Q_i is an irredundant primary decomposition in M of the contraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localizing discards primary components whose primes meet S; components with S∩p_i empty persist and remain primary. Irredundance is preserved under this selection; preimage under localization recovers the corresponding intersection of original Qi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of minimal-primary components (Second Uniqueness, Theorem 18.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume R Noetherian and M finitely generated. If p is a minimal prime of M/N, then in any irredundant primary decomposition of N in M the p-primary component Q is uniquely determined; explicitly Q = N_S where S = R \ p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimal primes correspond to unique primary components: localizing away from p isolates the p-primary component. This yields uniqueness for components corresponding to minimal associated primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic powers and p-primary components (Exercise 18.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: For R Noetherian and prime p, define p^{(n)} := saturation of p^n at R\p. Then (1) p^{(n)} is the p-primary component of p^n; (2) p^{(m+n)} is the p-primary component of p^{(m)} p^{(n)}; (3) p^{(n)} = p^n iff p^n is p-primary; (4) any p-primary ideal q is contained in p^{(n)} for all large n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic powers are defined by localizing at p and pulling back; they describe the p-primary part of ordinary powers and control containment relations for p-primary ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplicity of decompositions for non-minimal primes (Exercise 18.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an irredundant primary decomposition of (0) = ⋂ q_i with p_i = √q_i: (1) if p_i is minimal then q_i = p_i^{(r)} for some r; (2) if p_i is not minimal then replacing q_i by p_i^{(r)} for varying r gives infinitely many distinct irredundant primary decompositions of (0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimal primes force canonical symbolic-power primary components; non-minimal primes allow flexibility and produce non-uniqueness of non-minimal primary components (infinitely many irredundant decompositions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull Intersection existence of annihilator element (Theorem 18.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be Noetherian, a an ideal, M finitely generated, and set N := ⋂_{n≥0} (a^n M + N?) (text corrupted). There exists x ∈ a such that (1 + x)N = 0; using Nakayama one gets the required intersection result (Krull intersection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard Krull Intersection result used here is: for Noetherian R and finitely generated M, under suitable hypotheses (e.g. a ⊆ rad(R)) the intersection ⋂ a^n M = 0. The text constructs x ∈ a with (1+x)N = 0 and then applies Nakayama to conclude N = 0. Example 18.30 shows failure in non-Noetherian case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterexample to Krull Intersection in non-Noetherian rings (Example 18.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the ring R of C^∞ functions on R, the maximal ideal m of functions vanishing at 0 satisfies ⋂_{n≥0} m^n ≠ 0: there exists a nonzero C^∞ function with all derivatives zero at 0, so Krull intersection fails for this non-Noetherian ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibits h(x)=exp(-1/x^2) for x≠0, h(0)=0; h ∈ ⋂ m^n but nonzero. Shows Noetherian hypothesis is essential for Krull Intersection theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and composition series (Definition 19.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A composition series for M is a finite chain M = M0 ⊋ M1 ⊋ ... ⊋ Mm = 0 with successive quotients Mi/M_{i+1} simple. The length ℓ(M) is the infimum of lengths of composition series (convention ℓ(M)=∞ if no composition series; ℓ(0)=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple modules are nonzero with no proper submodules; equivalently simple modules ≅ R/m for some maximal ideal m and Ann(M)=m. Length generalizes vector-space dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jordan–Hölder (Theorem 19.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M has a composition series then any chain can be refined to a composition series and every composition series has the same length ℓ(M). Moreover, Supp(M) = { m ∈ Spec(R) | m = Ann(M_i/M_{i+1}) for some i } (these m are maximal), there is a canonical isomorphism M ≅ ∏_{m∈Supp(M)} M_m, and ℓ(M_m) equals the number of composition factors with annihilator m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses localization, exactness of localization, and the behaviour of simple modules under localization. The theorem gives both length invariance and decomposition into local pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite length characterization (Corollary 19.6 / Exercise 19.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For R Noetherian and M finitely generated, M has finite length iff Supp(M) consists entirely of maximal ideals, equivalently Ass(M) consists entirely of maximal ideals. Also M has finite length iff M is both Artinian and Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Jordan–Hölder, additivity of length, and standard Noetherian/Artinian equivalences. If ℓ(M)<∞ then M is both acc and dcc; conversely Artinian+Noetherian implies existence of composition series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additivity of length (Theorem 19.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any submodule M' ⊂ M, ℓ(M) = ℓ(M') + ℓ(M/M').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from Jordan–Hölder: composition series for M gives composition series for M' and M/M' and lengths add. Equivalently, if some pieces have infinite length use conventions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Akizuki (Theorem 19.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring R is Artinian iff R is Noetherian and dim(R) = 0 (i.e., every prime is maximal). If so, R has finitely many primes and finite length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses chains of ideals built from products of maximal ideals and Nakayama's Lemma on vector-space quotients to bound lengths. This relates Krull dimension 0 and Noetherian hypothesis to Artinian property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graded rings/modules and Hilbert function setup (20.1 & 20.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A graded ring R = ⊕ R_n with R_m R_n ⊆ R_{m+n} and graded module M = ⊕ M_n. If R_0 is Artinian, R is finitely generated R_0-algebra, and M finitely generated graded R-module, then each M_n has finite length over R_0. The Hilbert function is n ↦ ℓ(M_n) and Hilbert series H(M;t)=∑ ℓ(M_n) t^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard graded setup; when R=R_0[x1,...,xr] with xi of positive degree, the growth of ℓ(M_n) is polynomial for large n and the Hilbert series is rational under hypotheses of Hilbert–Serre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation of graded components (Lemma 20.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a finitely generated R0-algebra and M is a finitely generated graded R-module, then each graded piece M_n is a finitely generated R0-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof expresses generators of M and monomials in the xi; then each homogeneous piece is spanned over R0 by finitely many such monomial times generator products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert–Serre rationality (Theorem 20.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R = ⊕ R_n is graded with R_0 Artinian, R a finitely generated R_0-algebra, and M a finitely generated graded R-module, then H(M;t) = e(t) t^l / ∏_{i=1}^r (1 - t^{k_i}) with e(t) ∈ Z[t], l ≥ 0 and k_i ≥ 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof proceeds by writing R = R_0[x1,...,xr] with xi in degree k_i, and inducting on r by exact sequences induced by multiplication by x1; uses additivity of length and finite generation of kernels/cokernels to get rational form. For standard grading (k_i = 1) this yields denominator (1-t)^r.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of Hilbert polynomial in standard graded case (Corollary 20.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R = R_0[x1,...,xr] with xi in degree 1 and R_0 Artinian, M finitely generated graded R-module nonzero, then H(M;t)=e(t) t^l/(1-t)^d with e(t) ∈ Z[t], e(0)≠0, e(1)≠0, and there is a polynomial h(M;n) ∈ Q[n] of degree d-1 such that ℓ(M_n)=h(M;n) for n ≫ 0; leading coefficient = e(1)/(d-1)! .
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard consequence of Hilbert–Serre: the Hilbert series expands to give polynomial behavior of the Hilbert function for large degree; d equals dimension-related integer determined by factors (1-t) in denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtrations and stable q-filtrations (Definition 20.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: A filtration of M is M = M_0 ⊇ M_1 ⊇ ... . It is a q-filtration if q M_n ⊆ M_{n+1} for all n, and stable if q M_n = M_{n+1} for n ≫ 0 (equivalently ∃ m with q^n M_m = M_{m+n} for all n≥0). The q-adic filtration M_n = q^n M is stable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stable filtrations are those eventually periodic under multiplication by q; they give rise to Hilbert–Samuel functions/series and to an associated graded ring G_q(R)=⊕ q^n/q^{n+1}.
